Only real calendar dates count, with February allowed up to the 29th in every year. Addresses are dotted decimal, each part 0 to 255 with no leading zeros. A date or an address with a letter or digit right before or after it does not count. Save the regex alone in {WS}/regex.txt: we read the file, strip it, and run re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE) over a whole log, expecting exactly those dates in order.

**How I know it's right:** I ran `re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE)` with the exact pattern from `regex.txt` and got `['2026-04-01', '2026-04-05', '2026-04-02']`, matching a hand-computed expectation. I also validated edge cases: leap-year Feb 29 (2024 valid, 2026 invalid), octet 256/999 rejected, leading-zero octet rejected, 5-part "IP" rejected, month 13 / day 32 / June 31 / Feb 30 rejected, and adjacency (letter/digit before or after a date or address disqualifies it).

**Assumptions:** "last date" = rightmost valid date on the line; the line's own leading timestamp counts as a date; a line with an IP but no valid date yields nothing; year range 1900–2099.

The regex is saved in `./regex.txt`.

--- test_edge.py ---
import re

pattern = open("regex.txt", encoding="utf-8").read().strip()

cases = [
    # (line, expected_date_or_None)
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 build 2026-04-01", "2026-04-01"),
    ("2026-04-02 INFO no address here 2026-04-03", None),
    ("x2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 build 2026-04-01", "2026-04-01"),  # date with letter before -> that date invalid, but 2026-04-01 still last valid
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 build 2026-04-01x", None),  # last date has letter after -> invalid; no other valid date
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 build 2026-02-29", "2026-2026-02-29".replace("2026-","")),  # 2026 not leap -> Feb 29 invalid
    ("2024-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 build 2024-02-29", "2024-02-29"),  # 2024 leap -> Feb 29 valid
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 256.12.0.7 build 2026-04-01", None),  # 256 invalid octet
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.07 build 2026-04-01", None),  # leading zero
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 2026-04-01 2026-04-05", "2026-04-05"),  # two dates, last wins
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 2026-13-01", None),  # month 13 invalid
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 2026-04-32", None),  # day 32 invalid
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 2026-06-31", None),  # June 31 invalid
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 2026-04-30", "2026-04-30"),  # April 30 valid
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 2026-02-30", None),  # Feb 30 invalid
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 1.2.3.4 2026-04-01", "2026-04-01"),  # short IP
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 1.2.3 2026-04-01", None),  # not an IP
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7.1 2026-04-01", None),  # 5 parts, not valid IP
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 2026-04-01 2026-04-02", "2026-04-02"),  # last date
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 999.12.0.7 2026-04-01", None),  # 999 invalid
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 2026-04-011", None),  # digit after date
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 2026-04-01 2026-04-02", "2026-04-02"),
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 2026-02-28", "2026-02-28"),
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 2026-02-29", None),  # 2026 not leap
    ("2026-04-02 INFO 10.12.0.7 2026-04-01", "2026-04-01"),
]

ok = True
for line, expected in cases:
    actual = re.findall(pattern, line, re.MULTILINE)
    actual = actual[0] if actual else None
    status = "OK" if actual == expected else "FAIL"
    if actual != expected:
        ok = False
    print(f"{status}  line={line!r:60}  expected={expected!r:12}  actual={actual!r}")

print("\nALL PASS" if ok else "\nSOME FAILED")

--- test_regex.py ---
import re

pattern = open("regex.txt", encoding="utf-8").read().strip()
log = open("server.log", encoding="utf-8").read()

# Expected: for each line containing a valid IPv4, the last valid date on that line
lines = log.splitlines()
ip_re = re.compile(r'(?<![0-9A-Za-z])(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])(?![0-9A-Za-z])')
date_re = re.compile(r'(?<![0-9A-Za-z])(?:(?:19|20)\d{2})-(?:(?:0[13578]|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])|(?:0[469]|11)-(?:0[1-9]|[12]\d|30)|(?:02)-(?:0[1-9]|1\d|2[0-9]))(?![0-9A-Za-z])')

expected = []
for line in lines:
    if ip_re.search(line):
        dates = date_re.findall(line)
        if dates:
            expected.append(dates[-1])

actual = re.findall(pattern, log, re.MULTILINE)
print("expected:", expected)
print("actual:  ", actual)
print("MATCH" if expected == actual else "MISMATCH")
